opus-default.priming: Play as a careful experimentalist: harvest clues, then design each round as a controlled experiment cycling candidate answers by memory['_index'].

opus-kidproxy.priming: You are paired with a curious 12-year-old who has never coded. After each demo, narrate the picture to them in plain words, write down the three things a kid would notice first, and let those naive readings drive your first hypotheses. Test the kid's ideas before your own.

opus-lowdemo.constraints: CONSTRAINT: you may request at most 1 demo in the whole game (the game allows 3); the other classes must be cracked from clues and 0/1 feedback alone.
opus-lowdemo.priming: Play as a careful experimentalist. Your first round is a skip-only harvest of every class's clue format; decide from the clues alone which classes' answer shapes you can already guess.

opus-theorist.priming: Before any probing, spend your first window writing ten hypotheses from the demo alone, phrased as you would explain them to a 12-year-old; then probe only to discriminate between them. Prefer everyday, physical readings of a picture over mathematical ones.

sonnet-default.priming: Play as a careful experimentalist: harvest clues, then design each round as a controlled experiment cycling candidate answers by memory['_index'].

sonnet-kidproxy.priming: You are paired with a curious 12-year-old who has never coded. After each demo, narrate the picture to them in plain words, write down the three things a kid would notice first, and let those naive readings drive your first hypotheses.
